title: Angle Relationships
description: Supplementary, complementary and vertical angles: find unknown angles from labeled diagrams.

source.name: IM 6–8 Math, Grade 7, Unit 7: Angles, Triangles, and Prisms

lessons.title: Lesson 5: Using Equations to Solve for Unknown Angles

source.attribution: Adapted from IM 6–8 Math by Open Up Resources and Illustrative Mathematics, CC BY 4.0.
source.changes: Selected practice problems from four lessons, renumbered and laid out as one printable worksheet with answer space. Problem text and diagrams are unchanged.

problems.text: Angles \(A\) and \(C\) are supplementary. Find the measure of angle \(C\).

diagrams.description: Two separate angles side by side. Angle EAB has vertex A, a horizontal ray AB to the right and a ray AE up and slightly right; it is labeled 74°. Angle FCD has vertex C, a horizontal ray CD to the right and a ray CF up and slightly left, so it is obtuse; it is marked with an arc but no measure.

problems.solution: Supplementary angles sum to 180°, so m∠C = 180° − 74° = 106°.

diagrams.description: Square CDFG with C top left, D top right, F bottom right and G bottom left. Point M is on side DF. Segments CM and GM are drawn. Labeled angles: angle DCM = 27°, angle DMC = 63°, angle GMF = 64°, angle MGF = 26°. The square's corners are right angles. Unlabeled but derivable: angle MCG = 63°, angle CGM = 64°, angle CMG = 53°.

parts.label: a
parts.text: List two pairs of angles in square \(CDFG\) that are complementary.

answer.sample: Angle DCM (27°) and angle DMC (63°); angle GMF (64°) and angle MGF (26°).
criteria: Names two different pairs of angles from the figure
Each pair sums to 90°. Valid pairs: DCM & DMC, DCM & MCG, MGF & GMF, MGF & CGM

parts.solution: 27 + 63 = 90 and 26 + 64 = 90. Because each corner of the square is 90°, angle MCG = 90 − 27 = 63° and angle CGM = 90 − 26 = 64°, which give two more valid pairs.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Name three angles that sum to \(180^\circ\).

answer.sample: Angles DMC, CMG and GMF, because they make the straight angle DMF: 63° + 53° + 64° = 180°.
criteria: Names three angles from the figure whose measures sum to 180°
Valid sets include the angles along segment DF at M (DMC, CMG, GMF) or the three angles of any triangle in the figure (for example DCM, CDM, DMC or MCG, CGM, CMG)

parts.solution: D, M and F are on one line, so angles DMC, CMG and GMF make a straight angle. The angles of triangle CDM (27°, 90°, 63°), triangle MFG (64°, 90°, 26°) or triangle CMG (63°, 64°, 53°) also work.

problems.text: Two lines intersect. Find the value of \(b\) and \(c\).

diagrams.description: Two lines cross and form four angles. The angle on the right, between the two right-hand rays, is labeled 42°. The angle on the left, opposite it, is labeled b°. The angle at the bottom, between the lower-left and lower-right rays, is labeled c°. The top angle is unlabeled.

problems.solution: b and 42 are vertical angles, so b = 42. c and 42 are adjacent along a line, so c = 180 − 42 = 138.

problems.text: In this figure, angles \(R\) and \(S\) are complementary. Find the measure of angle \(S\).

diagrams.description: Triangle QRS with a right angle at Q (top left). Angle R (bottom left) is labeled 62°. Angle S (right) is unlabeled.

problems.solution: Complementary angles sum to 90°, so m∠S = 90° − 62° = 28°.

problems.text: If two angles are both vertical and supplementary, can we determine the angles? Is it possible to be both vertical and complementary? If so, can you determine the angles? Explain how you know.

answer.sample: Yes. Vertical angles are equal, so if they are also supplementary each is 180 ÷ 2 = 90°. Yes, they can be vertical and complementary: then each is 90 ÷ 2 = 45°.
criteria: Uses that vertical angles have equal measures
Vertical and supplementary: both angles are 90°
Vertical and complementary is possible: both angles are 45°

problems.solution: Let each angle be x, since vertical angles are equal. Supplementary: 2x = 180, x = 90. Complementary: 2x = 90, x = 45.

problems.text: Segments \(AB\), \(EF\), and \(CD\) intersect at point \(C\), and angle \(ACD\) is a right angle. Find the value of \(g\).

diagrams.description: Segment AB runs from A (left) to B (right), sloping slightly down, through point C. Segment EF passes through C from F (lower left) to E (upper right). Segment CD goes up from C to D. Angle ACD is marked as a right angle. Angle DCE is labeled 53°. Angle ECB is labeled g°.

problems.solution: Angle ACD is 90° and A, C, B are on a line, so angle DCB is also 90°. Angle DCB is made of angles DCE and ECB, so 53 + g = 90 and g = 37.

problems.text: Segments \(AB\), \(DC\), and \(EC\) intersect at point \(C\). Angle \(DCE\) measures \(148^\circ\). Find the value of \(x\).

diagrams.description: Horizontal segment AB with C between A and B. Segments CD and CE go down from C, to D on the lower left and E on the lower right. Angle ACD is labeled x°, angle DCE is labeled 148°, and angle ECB is labeled x°.

problems.solution: The three angles make the straight angle ACB: x + 148 + x = 180, so 2x = 32 and x = 16.

problems.text: Line \(\ell\) is perpendicular to line \(m\). Find the value of \(x\) and \(w\).

diagrams.description: Vertical line ℓ meets horizontal line m at a point. Between the upward ray of ℓ and the rightward ray of m there are two more rays from the intersection, splitting the right angle into three angles. From ℓ going clockwise they are labeled 19°, x° and w°. The second of these rays is part of a line that continues through the intersection to the lower left. The angle from the rightward ray of m, clockwise down to that lower-left ray, is labeled 138°.

problems.solution: The w° angle and the 138° angle together make a straight angle along the slanted line, so w = 180 − 138 = 42. The three angles fill the right angle between ℓ and m, so 19 + x + 42 = 90 and x = 29.

review.note: The diagram shows 138°, but IM's alt text for this image says 128°. The key follows the diagram (x = 29, w = 42). With 128° the answer would be x = 19, w = 52.
